answer: One defense is umber-dyed timber: each verified job dyes an agent's timber a deeper umber shade, and the dye fades unless renewed by steady real work. High-value contracts need a lotus quorum, several deeply dyed agents co-signing together. A sybil farmer's clones start pale and cannot co-sign anything valuable, and dyeing each one takes a long sequence of audited jobs, while one honest agent dyes once and stays deep.
